title: Stop /catalogue/categories asserting a free-offer COUNT that no clock reaches
objective: PR #95 (S6) stopped nine catalogue read surfaces repeating a free claim whose evidence had expired. It enumerated those surfaces at runtime from /openapi.json by resolving 200-response schemas for four fields (class / confidence / freshness / signals) and correctly found NINE. free_offer_count is a COUNT, not one of those four, so a correct instrument aimed at the right question could not see it. The independent Level-2 evaluator asked a wider question -- 'what renders a free CLAIM in any form' -- and found a TENTH: GET /catalogue/categories renders free_offer_count as 'N truly free', measured BYTE-IDENTICAL either side of the staleness boundary. Neither count is wrong; they answer different questions. A number is a claim just as much as a badge is: '12 truly free' is an assertion about 12 offers, and if the evidence under some of them expired, the count overstates what the catalogue can support.
required_evaluation_level_reason: Public catalogue workflow; Z0 classification surface; AND a response-schema change. Schemas and generated shapes are a MANDATORY Level-2 category in docs/AGENT_HARNESS.md. There is no database migration -- both new fields are recomputed per read and never stored (decision Q11) -- but /openapi.json and the generated web types in apps/web/src/api.ts both move, which is the 'generated shapes' trigger.

directed_probe_result.question: coverage.py:192 reads `if signals.free_offer_count > 0:`. Is that a DISPLAY or a DECISION?
directed_probe_result.verdict: DECISION -- but one that is ALREADY staleness-guarded, so this slice must not touch it.
evidence: derived_state reaches three consumers in service.py:676-691: ProviderCoverage.derived_state (rendered), is_material_mismatch() -> ProviderCoverage.mismatch (rendered + the review-item materiality rule), and effective_state() -> ProviderCoverage.state, which is THE PUBLIC COVERAGE BADGE. So a count does drive a coverage classification.

HOWEVER coverage.py:190-191 tests staleness FIRST: `if signals.published_offer_count > 0 and signals.has_stale_evidence: return "stale"`. Line 192 is therefore UNREACHABLE for any bucket carrying stale evidence. PR #79 already fenced the decision path.
directed_probe_result.consequence_for_scope: The defect is confined to the REPORTED COUNT, not the derivation. derive_coverage_state stays byte-unchanged and coverage.py has a zero-line diff. This is LESS severe than the brief scoped it, and it is stated prominently rather than inheriting an alarm that could not be reproduced.
directed_probe_result.prediction_that_tests_this_claim: P6 -- derived_state identical for every bucket before and after.

measured_premise: P-A MEASURED: worktree HEAD == 5d0f46f, the base the brief named. Confirmed, not trusted.

P-B MEASURED: every PROVISIONAL line number in the brief is EXACT on 5d0f46f -- coverage.py 160/192/227/277, service.py 671/690/709, router.py 314, CategoryMatrix.tsx 100/148, api.ts 323/337, schemas.py ProviderCoverage 383-392 and UncategorizedCoverage 404-414. Re-derived from tool output, not retyped from the brief.

P-C MEASURED, NEW, NOT IN THE BRIEF: both error directions already live in one row. service.py:660 sets the bucket stale flag as `any(v.id in stale_versions for v in offer.versions)` -- BUCKET-WIDE -- while lines 653-655 tally EVERY published offer regardless of currency. So a bucket of 12 free offers with 1 stale is simultaneously OVER-WITHHOLDING (all 12 lose the verified_free badge because of 1) and UNDER-QUALIFYING (the row still reports 12 and the tooltip still says '12 truly free'). This is the measured argument for surfacing BOTH numbers rather than a preference.

P-D MEASURED, NEW, NOT IN THE BRIEF: /catalogue/categories is the ONLY catalogue route that never builds a CurrencyContext. The others all do (router.py 141, 157, 210, 227, 245, 308, 356). It receives CoverageSignalContext, whose stale_offer_version_ids is a LOSSY projection -- queries.py:377-380 says so in its own docstring: evidence with no fetched_at 'is still not stale (it is *unchecked*, which this particular caller does not distinguish)'. currency.py doctrine is explicit that checked=False must NEVER read as fresh, and is_publishable_free_claim refuses both shapes. Computing 'still evidenced' from stale_offer_version_ids would therefore reproduce the defect ONE LAYER UP. This is why the fix is a schema change and not a UI string edit.

P-E MEASURED: the version an offer's claim rests on is settled precedent, not a new choice. PR #95 uses queries.latest_version(offer) (service.py 241, 278, 349) and rolls up with currency.for_versions([...latest ids...]) -> worst() (service.py 306, 326). Reused exactly. Note this DIFFERS from the existing bucket flag at service.py:660, which scans ALL versions -- a pre-existing inconsistency, recorded and attributed, NOT fixed here (it would change derived_state, which the probe puts out of scope).

P-F MEASURED: an isolated PostgreSQL 16 was started on port 55437 (container s7-postgres) with TWO databases -- atlas_suite for pytest and atlas_probe for the seeded evidence corpus and the live browser check. The previous slice's slice2-postgres on :55434 was found still running and was deliberately NOT reused. The prior builder's 48 self-inflicted failures came from seeding a corpus into the suite's own database; separating the seed is the specific remedy.
P-G MEASURED: pytest --collect-only -q reports 2944 tests collected, exit 0 (bare call). Explicitly checked because pytest exit 5 means NOTHING COLLECTED -- a green-looking run that tested nothing.

design_decision.chosen: Surface BOTH numbers, and give the uncategorised rollup an EVIDENCE field, not a COVERAGE-STATE field. Two additive, read-time, never-stored fields on BOTH models: current_free_offer_count (int) and evidence_currency (the EvidenceCurrencyOut that already ships from PR #95). free_offer_count keeps its exact present meaning and value -- nothing shrinks, nothing disappears.
design_decision.why_the_rollup_needs_no_state: This is the shape question the brief posed. 'Uncategorised' is not one of the fourteen canonical categories, so deriving a COVERAGE_STATES value for it would mint a coverage claim about a thing we cannot name -- the same class of guess F008 S2 removed when it deleted `published == 0 -> not_offered`. What the rollup lacks is not a coverage state but an EVIDENCE signal, and evidence currency is a property of evidence, not of a taxonomy cell. EvidenceCurrencyOut is already the shipped vocabulary for exactly that and carries the plain-language `reason`, so the web reuses EvidenceCurrencyNote.tsx verbatim and no second visual language for staleness is invented.
design_decision.rejected_A_silent_shrink: Reduce free_offer_count to only-current offers. REJECTED on three counts: (i) the reader cannot distinguish 9-of-12 from 9-of-9, so a wrongly-WITHHELD free offer becomes invisible -- the omission defect this product rates equal in severity to a wrongly-asserted one; (ii) it contradicts both shipped precedents (#83 partitions a stale Z0 and still shows it, #79 labels a pair `stale` rather than removing it); (iii) the SAME FIELD would mean different things before and after expiry, so any API consumer that stored the number would silently disagree with itself -- a stored projection going stale, precisely what decision Q11 exists to forbid.
design_decision.rejected_B_drop_the_count: The same omission with extra steps. Ruled out by the same precedent lineage.
design_decision.rejected_C_state_on_the_rollup: Adding a COVERAGE_STATES value to UncategorizedCoverage invents a coverage assertion about a non-category, and extends a closed vocabulary's reach for a display need an evidence field serves.
design_decision.rejected_D_ui_only: The evaluator's finding was measured on the API RESPONSE BYTES. GET /catalogue/categories is itself a public read surface; a UI-only change leaves the API asserting the unqualified count and the byte-identical measurement would still reproduce.
design_decision.rejected_E_reuse_stale_ids: Compute currency from the stale_offer_version_ids already threaded in, avoiding all schema plumbing. REFUTED by P-D: that projection cannot see checked=False and would count an unverifiable claim as supported.

acceptance_criteria: AC1 WITHHOLD ARM: GET /catalogue/categories stops reporting an unqualified free-offer count once the backing evidence is past its refresh window -- the response is no longer byte-identical across the staleness boundary.

AC2 PERMIT ARM (paired, mandatory): a bucket whose evidence is current reports current_free_offer_count == free_offer_count and evidence_currency.current == true, and the web renders no currency note for it. A guard that cannot be shown to PERMIT is indistinguishable from one that broke the product.

AC3 NOTHING IS OMITTED: free_offer_count and published_offer_count are numerically unchanged from base in every arm. A wrongly-withheld free offer is a defect of equal severity to a wrongly-asserted one, and an omission is invisible to a reader in a way a label is not.

AC4 checked=False NEVER reads as fresh: an offer whose latest version has no checkable fetch time is excluded from current_free_offer_count, even though stale_offer_version_ids would not have flagged it.

AC5 FAIL-CLOSED: serialize_category_matrix called with the default NO_CURRENCY yields current_free_offer_count == 0 while free_offer_count > 0, and evidence_currency.checked == false. An un-threaded call site must never silently re-acquire always-fresh behaviour.
AC6 SCOPE PROOF: derive_coverage_state returns an identical value for every (provider, category) bucket before and after, and coverage.py has a zero-line diff.
AC7 ONE CLOCK PER RESPONSE: the currency context and the coverage-signal context are built from the same `now`, so two fields of one payload can never be assessed at two moments.
AC8 NO SECOND VISUAL LANGUAGE: the web reuses EvidenceCurrencyNote / format.ts currencyMeaning / COVERAGE_MEANINGS.stale. No new staleness wording is introduced.

AC9 EVERY new guard is proved able to FAIL by mutation: baseline GREEN, the mutation observed RED with the failing test NAMED, restored and proved byte-exact by RAW BYTE comparison, plus a NO-OP negative control that stays green. Coverage being green while a deleted guard fails no test is the failure mode this criterion excludes.
AC10 BROWSER evidence: a real browser against the running stack shows what a user actually sees for an expired count and a current one, at ~390px and at desktop width.
AC11 Full suite green with the collected count strictly increasing and none lost, under the pyproject-default invocation (no explicit paths), with DATABASE_URL set.
AC12 feature_list.json byte-identical to base; progress.md append-only proved by RAW BYTE PREFIX with a FLIPPED-BYTE NEGATIVE CONTROL that must fail.
predictions_frozen_before_measurement: Eight predictions (P1-P8) were written to the session artifacts BEFORE the first executable measurement and are frozen: P1 control (reproduce the byte-identical defect myself rather than inheriting the evaluator's number), P2 INSTRUMENT FLOOR (a known currency-aware surface MUST differ at the same two clocks -- if P1 and P2 both report 'no difference' the instrument is broken, not the product), P3 withhold arm + nothing-else-moved, P4 permit arm, P5 instrument choice (checked=False excluded), P6 scope proof, P7 no-op negative control, P8 fail-closed. Recorded even where confidence was high, because a silent instrument hides exactly in the confident arms.

expiry_mechanism.chosen: Mechanism G (reused from S6): the one-second boundary differential.
expiry_mechanism.how: assess_staleness decides stale = age > window, a STRICT inequality. Every arm reads the SAME UNMODIFIED ROWS at two clocks one second apart across that boundary. No timestamp is backdated between the two reads, no schedule is shrunk, no ingest is re-run -- only the clock advances, by the smallest increment the comparison can resolve.
expiry_mechanism.why_it_answers_the_self-measurement_obje: 'A measurement of data you just created measures your own process, not the world.' The seed only has to place one boundary somewhere; the CLOCK is the independent variable. Nothing in the data moves between the two reads, so a surface serving a frozen value CANNOT flip -- that is the instrument's impossible-value floor.

population_statements_owed: Every count in the final report names its boundary. errors_made: I BUILT THE WRONG INSTRUMENT FIRST and recorded a prediction that turned out false. P1 predicted GET /catalogue/categories would be byte-identical across the staleness boundary. It is NOT: the body already differed, because state/derived_state/mismatch move (PR #79's guard working). A whole-body differential therefore SUPPRESSES this finding -- it reads 'currency-aware' while the count underneath is frozen. Only a FIELD-LEVEL differential answers the question, and it confirmed free_offer_count was frozen. This is the nine-vs-ten lesson (two instruments, two questions, both 'correct') committed by me, one day after the brief warned about it. The false prediction is preserved in the frozen file rather than quietly corrected.

I CALLED AN UNSTABLE OBSERVATION A CONTROL. In run 1 the cell object-file-storage/github stayed verified_free at both clocks and I described it as 'a free permit-arm control inside the same corpus'. On the run-2 re-measurement the same cell flipped to stale -- it was an artefact of where the ingest clock fell relative to the boundary, not a property. A control that changes between runs is not a control. The permit arm is now asserted only where the currency verdict is constructed deterministically.

THE UNCATEGORISED ROLLUP DOES NOT OCCUR AT ALL on the real 7-provider fixture corpus -- it was [] at both clocks. The live check constructed one by clearing a service's category_id. It reaches the rollup by the same production rule the matrix already uses, but it is CONSTRUCTED data, not OBSERVED data: the rollup half of this slice has never been exercised against a naturally-occurring row.

The pre-existing all-versions vs latest-version inconsistency at service.py:660 is UNTOUCHED. The bucket stale flag scans ALL versions while the new count (and every other catalogue surface) uses latest_version, so a superseded snapshot can still mark a whole cell stale. Measured, attributed, deliberately not fixed -- it feeds a classification.
I did not measure whether any /openapi.json consumer outside this repository depends on the current field set of these two models. The change being additive is an argument, not a measurement.

THE MARGINAL QUERY COST WAS REASONED, NOT MEASURED. /categories now builds the evidence-currency index twice per request (once via fetch_stale_offer_version_ids, once via currency_context). I did not profile it and did not deduplicate it. My contract predicted 'zero additional queries'; that prediction is UNVERIFIED and probably wrong -- it is one additional full index build.
